newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index soars to record 4,124.81 points.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index soars to record 4,124.81 points.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's (BSE) BUX index extended its gains on Monday, hitting the ninth successive record high, although Hungarian shares closed mixed.
The BUX finished at 4,124.81 points, up 22.34 points or 0.54 percent.

Traders said the BSE continued the trend of the past year when the BUX, with periods of downward corrections, soared from below 1,600 points in early January to above 4,100, mainly on good corporate and macroeconomic results.
"Looking at the medium term, I am still optimistic," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities. "There are stocks which still have potential for rising."
Traders said the trend was fuelled by demand from foreign investors, whose activity on the BSE was slack on Monday due to the year-end holidays.
As a result, and also because of profit-taking, Hungarian shares closed mixed, but gainers well outnumbered losers, and seven stocks even hit record highs.
The oil and gas company MOL, which rose much recently, closed down 10 forints at 2,005 forints, which traders attributed to profit-taking.
"I think MOL has the fundaments of further rise," said Attila Gazdik of New York Broker. "But it cannot go up 100 forints every day."
The retail company Fotex firmed 11 forints to 100.

Traders said Fotex's rise may have been triggered by a newspaper report that investors had subscribed $2.54 million worth of Fotex bonds and expectations that the demand for retail goods would strengthen in Hungary next year.

BUX index futures rose, except for the June 1998 maturity, which dropped 16.50 points, to end at 5015. The December 1997 maturity closed at 4,777.50 points, up 37.00, while December 1998 BUX futures ended at 5,340.50, up 30.50.
